gcp_cloud_logging_confirmation.basis_for_proceeding: Circumstantial, not log-confirmed: infra/deploy.sh's gcloud run deploy taal-agents call (verified by direct file read) sets no --memory/--cpu/--concurrency, so it runs on Cloud Run's default (512 MiB, 1 vCPU, concurrency 80); local peak RSS on the stub backend alone (measured below) is 198.8 MiB single-request, and the deployed service also carries FastAPI/uvicorn baseline overhead, ADK agent state, and concurrent-request multiplication (concurrency 80 means up to 80 requests can share that 512 MiB instance); the 503 arrives after several seconds of real work (6.75s and 12.8s), consistent with a request completing enough server-side work to get killed rather than an immediate connection-refused. This is a plausible, not proven, memory-exhaustion story. User was asked and explicitly chose to proceed on this basis rather than wait for a confirmed root cause.

local_memory_measurement.discrepancy_with_task_evidence: The task's own evidence states 'Locally the uvicorn worker peaks at 481 MiB during three stub-backend approves.' This measurement, run the same way (stub backend, 3 approves), found 198.8 MiB peak on the actual worker process -- not 481 MiB. The two numbers were not reconciled: possible explanations (an uncontrolled --reload subprocess doubling memory, a different warm/cold cache state, measuring the wrong process as this session's first attempt did) were not chased down further. Reporting both numbers rather than picking one.
local_memory_measurement.conclusion: Even taking the higher, unreconciled 481 MiB figure at face value, it already exceeds Cloud Run's 512 MiB default's usable headroom under any concurrent load (concurrency 80 default). This session's own 198.8 MiB reading is a stub-backend, single-worker, sequential-request floor -- it does not by itself prove 512 MiB is insufficient under live Vertex calls and real concurrency, which is why memory was raised to 2Gi rather than to a value just above either measured number.

cost_delta.billing_model: Cloud Run request-based billing (min-instances stays 0 on both services -- unchanged by this PR): CPU and memory are billed only for the duration of an actual request (plus a brief idle-instance grace period after), never while the instance is scaled to zero.
cost_delta.taal-agents: 512 MiB/1 vCPU -> 2 GiB/2 vCPU is a 4x memory-seconds and 2x vCPU-seconds rate during request-serving time only. At Cloud Run's list pricing (~$0.0000025/vCPU-second, ~$0.0000025/GiB-second as of the prices used elsewhere in this repo's cost analysis, docs/DECISIONS.md §18.4), a single ~2-8s Planner/approve call goes from roughly $0.00001-0.00002 to $0.00006-0.00012 -- a few hundredths of a cent per call. At the judge/demo traffic volumes this repo is built for (tens to low hundreds of calls/day), the total delta is well under $1/month.
cost_delta.taal-web: default (256-512 MiB depending on Cloud Run's current default) -> 1 GiB is a similarly small per-request delta; taal-web serves static/SSR pages, not long model calls, so its total cost contribution stays negligible.
cost_delta.net: No new idle/always-on cost (min-instances unchanged at 0). The entire delta is a small multiplier on already-small per-request compute charges.
